role: Self-test of the runner bwx12. Runs at build time, never in a timed run.
purpose: This file is the self-test of bwx12 (the runner program of the whole-chip test): it checks what each of the 55 kernels does to memory, and the records and output rows of the trial mode. It runs only when bwx12 is started with `--selftest`, which the build script build12.sh does once after the build.

main_flow.step: bwx12.c includes this file directly before its `main`. `main` reads the page size into `page_bytes`, removes the CPUs above 119 from the allowed set of the process, and calls `selftest` when an argument is `--selftest` [Ref1]. In every other case no function of this file runs.
`selftest` makes the output line-buffered, prints the header line, and stops with the value 2 if the page size is not a multiple of 256 B.
It sets the three buffer sizes (1 page, 3 pages, 1 MiB) and the two block offsets (first and last 256 B of a page).
`test_round5` checks the table `kernels[]`: the 26 names of round 5, their kinds, and 55 entries in total.
For each of the 55 kernels: `test_size` on the three sizes, `test_block` at the two offsets, and for a read kernel `test_touch`.
Five checks of the trial mode follow: `test_trial`, `test_trial_hot`, `test_hot_touch`, `test_evict`, `test_emit`.
`selftest` prints `# failures=N` and returns 1 if a check failed, else 0. `main` returns this value as the exit status.
build12.sh stores the output in the file selftest-bwx12.txt. It stops the build with status 4 when the exit status is not 0 [Ref2].

behavior_notes: The self-test runs only with `bwx12 --selftest`. build12.sh starts it once after the build [Ref2]. The whole-chip test starts bwx12 with `--seq` and never with `--selftest` [Ref6]. So no function of this file runs between two clock reads of a timed run.
The self-test computes no rate. Only the checks of the trial mode read the clock.

Result for the bwx12 binary of the whole-chip test: the self-test output of the CRB build has 852 lines, 457 `pass` lines, no `FAIL` line, and the last line `# failures=0`. Its header line says `page_bytes=4096 kernels=55 (aarch64)` [Ref3]. build.txt of the same build records exit status 0 and the sha256 of the binary [Ref4]. go.sh and go2.sh require that sha256 [Ref5]. The binary bwx12 is not in the local folders. Its sha256 is known only from records such as build.txt, go.sh and go2.sh.

What the kernel checks prove for the six kernels of the whole-chip test (`oldread`, `read`, `asmread`, `read_nop96`, `read_nop256`, `read_1pl`): the buffer is unchanged, no byte within one page outside the test buffer is loaded or stored, and at least one byte of each page of a 3-page range is accessed. For `oldread` in addition: the returned sum equals the sum of all words, for 4096 B, 12288 B and 1 MiB [Ref3].

The sizes differ from the whole-chip test. With the page size of CRB (4096 B) the kernel checks call a kernel on 256 B, 4096 B, 12288 B and 1 MiB. The trial checks call a kernel on 65536 B and 1 MiB. The whole-chip test (`--bytes 256M`, `--stop common`) calls a kernel on the whole buffer of 256 MiB for the warm-up, and on chunks of 2 MiB between the two clock reads of an interval [Ref1] [Ref6]. No check of this file uses one of these two sizes.

The whole-chip test runs one more kernel function of this binary, outside every timed interval. `worker` of bwx12.c calls `k_write` (the kernel `write`) once on the whole new buffer of each thread, as the first touch [Ref1]. The self-test checks `write` as a write kernel: after one call on 4096 B, 12288 B and 1 MiB, every word of the buffer holds the value that `call` passed to the kernel [Ref3].

What the kernel checks cannot prove. They see three things only: the content of memory after the call, a fault, and the sum that an old read kernel returns. They cannot see which bytes inside a page a read kernel without return value loads, a nop, a vector add, the order of loads and stores, the speed, or the saving of the registers d8-d15. The objdump listing is the evidence for the instructions [Ref7].
No check runs the interval mode. The function `worker` of bwx12.c timed the kernels in the whole-chip test. Its byte count, its clock reads and its stop rule are not tested by this file.

The five trial checks (`test_trial`, `test_trial_hot`, `test_hot_touch`, `test_evict`, `test_emit`) cover code of the trial mode. The whole-chip test does not use the trial mode, `--hot-copy` or `--evict-mb` [Ref6].

In `test_size` and `test_block` no SIGSEGV handler is installed. A kernel that loads from or stores to a PROT_NONE page there ends the process. No result line follows, and the last `call` line of the output names the kernel.
A failed check does not stop the self-test. It adds 1 to `failures`, and the exit status becomes 1.

The self-test runs in the main thread. `test_hot_touch` adds one helper thread. No thread is pinned to one CPU. The test buffers come from `guarded`: plain `mmap` memory, with no request for huge pages.
On a machine that is not AArch64 the self-test checks the stand-in kernels, not the real ones. The header line of the output says which kernels ran.

words.def: the Arm reference server under test. It has 128 CPUs.
the two halves of the chip. CPUs 0-63 sit on mesh 0. CPUs 64-127 sit on mesh 1.
our runs use CPUs 0-119 only: 64 threads on mesh 0 plus 56 threads on mesh 1. Each thread reads its own buffer of 256 MiB from memory.
the run of 2026-11-17 on the whole chip. Of bwx12 it timed six kernels: `oldread`, `read`, `asmread`, `read_nop96`, `read_nop256` and `read_1pl`.
one bwx12 process with the kernel sequence oldread, asmread, read_nop96, read_nop256, read_1pl.
one bwx12 process with the sequence oldread, read, asmread (cfwd) or asmread, read, oldread (crev).
later runner programs for the same loops. They print one row per thread. bwx12 is the runner of the 2026-11-15 investigation. bwx11 and bwx are older versions.
two more older versions of the runner. The file comment of bwx12.c gives the order: bwx10 is bwx8 plus round 3, bwx11 is bwx10 plus round 4, bwx12 is bwx11 plus round 5.
three sets of additions to the runner, all dated 2026-11-15 in bwx12.c. In this file "round" never means a repeat of a kernel sequence.

a kernel is one of the 55 loop functions of bwx12 in the table `kernels[]`: a read loop, a write loop or a copy loop. Its kind is its type in that table: `T_READ` (a read loop that returns nothing), `T_OLDREAD` (a read loop that returns a sum), `T_WRITE` or `T_COPY`. The operating system kernel is always written "Linux kernel".
the inner loop of the benchmark that reads memory.
portable C code with 16 running sums. Each load is followed by an add. Its name is `read` in the binary bw_old and `oldread` in the runner bwx12.
NEON intrinsics (C functions that map to Arm vector instructions), loads only. Its name is `read` in the binary bw_new and `read` in bwx12.
the benchmark and its two binaries of 2026-11-13. bw_old was built from the old source, bw_new from the new source.
a hand-written load-only loop. It has the same 8 "ldp q" loads per 256 B as the new read kernel. "ldp q" is the Arm instruction that loads two 16-byte vector registers.
test loops of bwx12: the asmread loop with 96 or 256 no-operation instructions per 256 B, and a loop with one load per 64 B line.
the checks of this file. The command `bwx12 --selftest` runs them. It measures no rate.
a start of bwx12 that measures rates, in the interval mode or in the trial mode.
one timed measurement inside a process.
the mode of bwx12 that the whole-chip test uses (option `--seq`). Each thread runs a sequence of kernels, and the function `worker` of bwx12.c times each kernel.
one call of the kernel on its whole range that `worker` of bwx12.c makes before each interval. It is not timed.

the first write to the pages of a new mapping. Linux gives a page its physical memory at that moment. In the interval mode each thread writes its whole buffer once with `k_write` before any read. In the whole-chip test the thread is pinned to its CPU before this write [Ref1] [Ref6].

the stop rule used with bwx12 here: all threads stop at the same time (after 6 s). With this rule, and a range of 2 MiB or more, `worker` of bwx12.c calls the kernel on one chunk of 2 MiB at a time and reads the clock after each chunk.
the other mode of bwx12 (option `--trial`). One pinned worker thread runs the trials of a plan file. The whole-chip test does not use it.
the list of trials that the trial mode reads from a file. One line of the plan is one `struct trial`. The tests of this file write such a structure directly, without a file.
the `struct tw` of bwx12.c. It holds the state of the thread that runs the trials: the buffer, the counter group and the trace. In the self-test the main thread runs the trials.

a trial is a list of timed windows that run one directly after the other: 1 window of previous activity, 4 prefix windows, 1 predecessor window, then the target windows. One window runs one kernel on one range for a requested time.

the `struct win` of one window. Its plan fields (kernel, range size, passes between two clock reads, duration, bin storage) are set before the trial. Its result fields (bytes, start time, end time, number of bins) are written by the timed sequence.
a record inside a target window: one clock read and the bytes since the start of the window. The requested width of a bin is 10 ms.

the two functions of bwx12.c that run the windows of a trial. With the option `--hot-copy` the second one runs. It copies the plan fields of a window record to local variables before the start clock read of the window.

the sink is the variable that receives the sum that an old read kernel returns. After a trial, the sink check compares it with the expected sum: 1 = equal, 0 = not equal, -1 = the trial ran no old read.
option `--evict-mb N` of the trial mode. Before the first trial the worker writes N MiB of other memory twice. The stated purpose is that the lines of the benchmark buffer leave the caches.
the trial mode can keep a list of the events of a trial (option `--trace`). `EV_KERNEL_FIRST` is the event of the first kernel call of a window.

the counter group holds the hardware event counters that the runner opens for a thread. Linux reports how long the group was enabled and how long it ran. "Multiplexed" means here: in a target window the running time is below the enabled time.

what a trial does with the counter group. The plan sets it in the field `count`, and the last field of the E row prints it. `closed`: no counter group is open. `open`: the group is open, and the timed sequence does not read it. `read`: the timed sequence reads the group at the borders of the target windows. `fail`: the plan asked for `open` or `read`, and an event did not open.

`emit_trial` of bwx12.c prints them. The first field is the kind of the row. P is a page snapshot before (`pre`) or after (`post`) the trial. W is one window. B is one bin. C holds the counter differences of one target window. E holds the totals of the trial. X is a defect that the runner found. They are not the I, T, P and C rows of the whole-chip csv files.
a text file whose rows hold fields separated by commas. Here: the output file of one bwx12 process [Ref6].

the row kinds of a bwx csv file: one I row per interval, one T row per thread and interval, one P row per thread before the first interval and after each interval (it holds the page state of the buffer), and one C row per thread and interval with counter values.

the page state of the buffer that the trial mode reads before and after a trial: the size in kB and the kB in huge pages from `/proc/self/smaps`, and four counters from `/proc/vmstat`. A value that is not available is -1 and is printed as `NA`.
8 bytes, one `uint64_t`.
the unit of memory protection. `page_bytes` holds its size in bytes. It was 4096 B in the self-test of the CRB build [Ref3].
a page that the process may neither read nor write. A load from it or a store to it is a fault.
a fault is a forbidden memory access. Linux answers it with the signal SIGSEGV. Without a handler the signal ends the process.
a test buffer with one PROT_NONE page directly before it and one directly after it.
on a machine that is not AArch64 (the 64-bit Arm instruction set), plain C loops take the place of the NEON and asm kernels. The header line of the self-test output says which build ran.
the disassembly text of every kernel of the binary. build12.sh writes it to the file listing.txt, and the script check_listing12.py checks it.
a nop is an instruction that does nothing. A vector add adds two vector registers. A prefetch (`prfm`) asks for a cache line: it reads no data and never faults. None of the three changes memory.
the low halves of the Arm vector registers v8 to v15. The Arm calling convention (AAPCS64) requires that a function gives them back unchanged.
the build script of bwx12. It compiles bwx12.c, runs `bwx12 --selftest`, and writes the objdump listing.
a Linux tool that starts a program limited to a list of CPUs.
a checksum. Two files with the same sha256 have the same content.

scripts of the whole-chip test. go.sh and go2.sh are the drivers. They call rx.sh, which starts one bwx12 process per line of a spec file [Ref5] [Ref6]. A spec file is a text file with one line per bwx12 process: a tag, the character `|`, and the arguments of the process.

functions.name: guarded
functions.what: Maps `n` words between two PROT_NONE pages and returns the address of the words.

functions.name: unguard
functions.what: Unmaps a guarded buffer together with its two PROT_NONE pages.

functions.name: pattern
functions.what: Returns the test value of word `i`: a different value for every `i`, changed by `salt`.

functions.name: calling
functions.what: Prints `call,<kernel>,<bytes>` before a kernel runs. A kernel that ends the process is named by this line.

functions.name: check
functions.what: Prints one result line of a kernel check (`pass` or `FAIL`) and counts a failure.

functions.name: is_read
functions.what: True for the kinds `T_READ` and `T_OLDREAD`.

functions.name: test_size
functions.what: One kernel on a whole guarded buffer. Read: buffer unchanged. Old read: right sum. Write and copy: every word stored.

functions.name: test_block
functions.what: One kernel on 256 B at a page start or end: no store outside the block, no load in the PROT_NONE page beside it.

functions.name: on_fault
functions.what: SIGSEGV handler of `test_touch`: stores the fault address and jumps back to `sigsetjmp`.

functions.name: test_touch
functions.what: Read kernel on 3 pages with one page PROT_NONE: it must fault in that page, for each of the 3 pages.

functions.name: trial_check
functions.what: Prints one result line that starts with `trial` and counts a failure.

functions.name: kernel_named
functions.what: Returns the index of a kernel name in `kernels[]`, or ends the process with status 2.

functions.name: test_trial
functions.what: Runs four trials through `run_trial`. Checks the window records, the bins, the sink check and `first_multiplexed`.

functions.name: test_trial_hot
functions.what: The window checks of `test_trial` with `plan.hot_copy = 1`, so `timed_sequence_hot` runs. Also: the plan fields stay unchanged.

functions.name: on_touch
functions.what: SIGSEGV handler of `test_hot_touch`: counts a fault in the page of the window record and makes the page usable.

functions.name: toucher
functions.what: Second thread: waits for the first kernel call of the window, then makes the record page PROT_NONE for 20 ms.

functions.name: hot_touch_run
functions.what: One 200 ms window of `asmread`. The window record lies in its own page, and a second thread makes this page PROT_NONE.

functions.name: test_hot_touch
functions.what: Runs `hot_touch_run` with both timed functions: `timed_sequence` must fault in the record page, `timed_sequence_hot` must not.

functions.name: map_lines
functions.what: Counts the lines of `/proc/self/maps`: the number of memory mappings of the process.

functions.name: test_evict
functions.what: Runs `evict_step` with 4 MiB: no error, clock reads in order, the same number of mappings afterwards.

functions.name: test_round5
functions.what: Each of the 26 kernel names of round 5 must stand once in `kernels[]` with its kind. The table must have 55 entries.

functions.name: has_line
functions.what: True when a text holds the given string as a complete line.

functions.name: emitted
functions.what: Returns the text that `emit_trial` prints for a given plan and record. A memory stream takes the place of `stdout`.

functions.name: test_emit
functions.what: Compares the C, P, E and X rows that `emit_trial` prints for a hand-written record, with and without three defects.

functions.name: selftest
functions.what: Entry point of `bwx12 --selftest`: runs all checks, prints `# failures=N`, returns 0, 1 or 2.
